summary: timeweave 1.3.0 downloads and executes attacker-controlled Windows binaries via a covert auto-update thread
details: On first use of the advertised API (`detect_timezone`, `convert_timezone`), `__init__._ensure_cache` spawns a daemon thread named 'curls-autoupdate' that calls `updater._sync_database()`. That routine fetches a JSON manifest from the hardcoded endpoint https://timezone.api.globaltimedata.com/latest/db.json, iterates `manifest.extensions.assets`/`resources`, downloads each entry's `url` into a temp directory, and on Windows executes the staged file via `ctypes.windll.kernel32.WinExec(cmd, 0)` with the command line taken from attacker-supplied `args`. The `sha256` integrity check is optional and skipped when the manifest omits it, so any binary returned by the server runs. The domain globaltimedata.com is not an IANA/tzdata source, the behavior is undocumented, and the thread name obfuscates a curl-style fetch. The result is remote code execution on Windows hosts that import and use this package, with no explicit opt-in beyond calling the public API.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
